text: In 1970, Oregon tried to get rid of a dead whale with dynamite.
It did not get rid of the whale.
A forty-five foot, eight-ton sperm whale had washed up on a beach near Florence.
Nobody knew how to move it, and it was starting to smell.
So the job went to the Highway Department.
Their engineer decided to treat it like a boulder, and blow it up with half a ton of dynamite.
The plan: blast the whale into tiny pieces, and let the seagulls eat the rest.
A crowd gathered on the dunes.
Huge chunks of blubber rained down on the crowd.
One crushed a car parked nearly a quarter mile away.
And most of the whale was still lying right there on the beach.
So the highway crew did the one thing they'd been trying to avoid.
Today, that beach is a park named after the exploding whale.
